audience: An operator studying how deterministic workflow graphs and coding agents should divide software-engineering work.
problem: A strong coding model is often asked to spend inference on setup, routing, retries, and validation that ordinary software can perform more reliably, while design-oriented app builders can be fast at scaffolding but weak at hard debugging.
solution: A study lab that pins existing OSS and project references, reuses a mature frontend substrate, makes deterministic graph edges explicit, and invokes a coding worker only on unresolved semantic failures.

evidence.claim: The executable workflow grants success only when deterministic validation returns ok; the coding worker can propose a repair but cannot mark a run successful.
evidence.source: src/graph_study/flow.py, the Validate node, at commit ac985d31e16272186115903ecddf9072356595d6.
evidence.supports: Validate.run branches on ValidationEvidence.ok and reaches _finish("passed") only on a zero-exit validator; Repair is the single inference edge.
evidence.limits: A source read does not prove the graph ran on any particular machine; local run evidence is recorded separately from the code.

evidence.claim: Bare command names such as pnpm are resolved through PATH and PATHEXT before execution, so Windows .CMD shims run instead of failing with WinError 2.
evidence.source: src/graph_study/actions.py, the _resolve_executable helper, at commit ac985d31e16272186115903ecddf9072356595d6.
evidence.supports: _resolve_executable calls shutil.which(argv[0]) and substitutes the resolved path, which is why the default validator no longer returns 127 on Windows.
evidence.limits: The fix is platform-independent by construction, but the recorded reproduction came from a single Windows machine.

evidence.claim: The repository owner authorized completing this adopter content surface and enabling auto-merge that needs no stored credential.
evidence.source: Owner instruction recorded during the 2026-10-05 working session on this repository.
evidence.supports: Explains why the study repository carries a content-system adapter and a token-only auto-merge workflow at all.
evidence.limits: A recorded decision is not proof that either path works; the workflow's own runs and the local hotload are the separate evidence.

boundaries: GitHub repository setup is not proof that local Docker, Node, browser, or coding-agent runs succeed.
No paid model is required on the baseline path.
Downloaded source checkouts remain local and are not vendored into git.
